reviewed_conventions.lesson: Use moment sequence for an indexed sequence of moments. If using Stieltjes, show the nonnegative measure on[0,∞) or the corresponding criterion, with its hypotheses.
reviewed_conventions.source_observation: The source names Toeplitz and Hankel matrices first, then defines Stieltjes moment sequences and displays the measure representation.
reviewed_conventions.limit: The donor after text uses only moment sequences, which is appropriately weaker. This source does not verify the target determinants, strict positivity, determinacy or rational-function claim.

reviewed_conventions.lesson: Call a finite sum of the series terms a partial sum, distinguish it from the full sum and the remainder, and state the integer produced by the next argument.
reviewed_conventions.source_observation: The source explicitly introduces the full sum a and partial sums s_n, then names the fractional remainder and denominator-clearing integer in the constructive application.
reviewed_conventions.limit: A prefix of a continued fraction remains a prefix. The source supplies terminology and an explanatory pattern; it does not validate the target finite calculation or infinite condition.

reviewed_conventions.lesson: Use the established k-kernel name for the family of decimated subsequences; define the family and finiteness criterion. Keep Yazdani’s Shallit credit adjacent to a reused separation construction.
reviewed_conventions.source_observation: The source defines k-automatic by finiteness of the k-kernel, explains the base-k finite-state-machine meaning, and attaches Shallit credit immediately before Theorem2. The proof then selects a reduced progression before using Dirichlet.
reviewed_conventions.limit: A private relation module or explicit evaluation matrix can be described directly; this source does not give those objects a new standard name. This is not a complete check of whether every part of the target construction is inherited.

reviewed_conventions.lesson: When importing an expansion, write the residual equation and its numerator/denominator before deriving the integrality consequence. Distinguish a remainder from its numerator.
reviewed_conventions.source_observation: The published passage introduces the rational residual x_n, writes it as c_n/d_n, then derives the grid on which the next error lies. This provides an actual coordinate explanation rather than a slogan about a construction.
reviewed_conventions.limit: The local PDF is the published2026 paper, whereas the source archive and arXiv URL identify an earlier2025 source. The exposition analogy is not proof authority for a different claim.

reviewed_conventions.lesson: Define the combined nonnegative quantity, bound its average or minimum, and then select one index that controls every term needed next.
reviewed_conventions.source_observation: The source sums the distinguished coefficient and shifted tail terms into µ_{k,i}, estimates the sum across progression samples, defines a minimum τ_k, and chooses i_k attaining that minimum. The same chosen n_k then appears in both inequalities(2.9).

reviewed_conventions.lesson: Name the components, what each component’s numbers count, and whether multiplicity is included before applying the covering identity.
reviewed_conventions.source_observation: The source defines critical points and values with multiplicity, names Ω_j components and their d_j and r_j counts, and only then states the covering/Riemann–Hurwitz equality.
reviewed_conventions.limit: The proposition assumes a smooth lemniscate. Its count convention and writing pattern do not prove an unrestricted statement about arbitrary connected sets.

reviewed_conventions.lesson: Specify projection maps and image sets, prove the per-piece estimate, and explain the multiplicity bound used when adding the pieces.
reviewed_conventions.source_observation: The source introduces π_x and π_y as orthogonal projections;Lemma2 states an analytic-curve intersection bound, and its proof explains per-piece inequalities and at-most-n-to-one projection counts. The abstract separately says connectedness is an ingredient for an extremal polynomial.
reviewed_conventions.limit: A schematic of an arbitrary connected K must not silently make K a rectifiable path or copy the analytic-curve hypothesis. Extremal connectedness is an ingredient with its own domain.

reviewed_conventions.lesson: After the inductive choice preserves the finite-remainder condition, say that the construction step is complete. Then explicitly invoke convergence of the endpoint bounds to identify the infinite sum.
reviewed_conventions.source_observation: The source maintains x−sum_{n≤N}x_n∈[a_N,b_N], chooses x_{N+1}, and then uses convergence a_N,b_N→0 to conclude x=sum_n x_n. It visibly separates the finite invariant from the infinite conclusion.
reviewed_conventions.limit: This is the strongest companion example for the current draft because the cited argument actually exhibits the distinction. The target paper still needs its own preserved invariant and limiting hypothesis.
